X.note: The globe render is attractive, but the frame doesn't match what it says. The caption says 'Cities may allow single-stair buildings' while the map highlights only Texas, and there is no route or movement, so it reads as a location pin. The callout is a long single line of small text and is the weak point on a phone. The Sources line is tiny and low-contrast. The 'As of' chip and 'ACTUAL' badge are small and unexplained. The wide view of Mexico and the Caribbean wastes space. Texas is orange on a brown-green landscape, so it stands out only moderately.

Y.note: The relief map is clean and the route is easy to follow: Buffalo, across the state, to Albany, then down to New York. The place labels are large, high-contrast white on dark, so they read on a phone. The farmer and boat figures are small but they carry the story. The caption is clear and spans two lines. Weaknesses: the Hudson leg is a thin dashed line that is hard to see. The labels sit a little off their points, for example Genesee Valley's pointer hangs below the figure. The route line is thin and blends into the terrain. The Erie Canal itself is not labeled.

why: Y shows an actual route with large, legible labels and a caption that matches the map, while X is a pretty globe with one small text-heavy callout that has little to do with its caption.
top_fix_for_weaker: For X, make the single-state callout big and short (for example 'TEXAS: single-stair up to 6 floors'). Zoom the camera in on the US and highlight every state that has passed the rule, so the map matches the caption. Drop or explain the 'As of' chip and 'ACTUAL' badge, and enlarge and darken-back the source line.
